tagline: Gravel through the Tendoys, with trout in view of the car.
intro: From Interstate 15 at Dell the Tendoy Mountains look impenetrable. A frontage road and then Big Sheep Creek Road find the way in, a gravel byway of some 50 miles that runs up Big Sheep Canyon, across a broad valley framed by mountains along the Continental Divide, and north through the Medicine Lodge valley to Highway 324 near Clark Canyon Reservoir.
BLM figures three hours for the drive. Once past the canyons, a traveler may meet only two or three cars along the entire route.
season: Visit Montana says the road can be driven safely from May through early October.

moments.title: Dell
moments.text: Founded as a station on the Utah and Northern Railway and home to 17 people at the 2020 census, Dell gets the lightest precipitation in Montana.

moments.title: Big Sheep Canyon
moments.text: Under high rock cliffs the road looks down into clear, deep pools of spring-fed Big Sheep Creek, and perhaps nowhere else in America can one see so many trout without leaving the car.

moments.title: Medicine Lodge valley
moments.text: The last thirty miles or so follow a meandering creek through the Medicine Lodge valley, under the peak that gives it the name.

practical: Two-lane gravel with a short one-lane dirt stretch and no potable water, and BLM advises planning fuel stops in advance. Portions are impassable when wet, and travelers are asked to shut the gates they pass through.
